title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 141 (Eligibility, qualifications and disqualifications of auditors)

content.overview: A person shall be eligible for appointment as an auditor of a company only if he is a chartered accountant. A firm including a limited liability partnership of which majority of partners practising in India are qualified for appointment as aforesaid may be appointed by its firm name to be auditor of a company. Section 141(3) sets out disqualifications including a body corporate other than an LLP, an officer or employee of the company, a person indebted beyond the prescribed amount, and other specified relationships and security holdings.
content.glance: Only a chartered accountant (or a firm with a majority of CA partners practising in India) may be appointed auditor, subject to the disqualifications in section 141(3).
content.study:
## Section 141 — Eligibility and disqualifications

**Eligibility.** A person is eligible only if he is a chartered accountant. A firm (including an LLP) whose majority of partners practising in India are so qualified may be appointed by firm name.

**Disqualifications (subsection (3)).** Include among others: body corporate other than an LLP; officer or employee of the company; partner or employee of an officer or employee; person indebted to the company or related companies beyond the prescribed amount; person who has given a guarantee for such indebtedness; person holding security of or interest in the company as the section describes; person in full-time employment elsewhere; and holding appointment in more than the prescribed number of companies.

**Effect.** Appointment in contravention is void; a disqualification arising after appointment vacates the office.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.
